questions.question: Two independent fair coin indicators both take values $0$ and $1$ with the same probabilities. What can be true?
options: Same Bernoulli distribution, but not the same random variable.
Same Bernoulli distribution, so they always take equal values.
Different distributions, since independent variables cannot share one.
Their sum also has a Bernoulli distribution with parameter $1/2$.

questions.question: If $X$ has the same distribution as $Y$, can observing $X$ and observing $Y$ still be different experiments?
options: Yes; same distribution need not mean the same random variable.
No, same distribution makes them the same function on the same $S$.
Yes, but only if $X$ and $Y$ are independent of each other.
Yes, but only if their supports are different sets of values.

questions.question: What is the distribution of a random variable $X$ defined on a probability space $(S,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$?
options: The function $X\colon S\to\mathbb{R}$ itself, mapping outcomes to values
The set of values that $X$ can take with positive probability
The probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ assigning $\mathbb{P}(X\in B)$ to suitable sets $B$
The sample space $S$ together with its probability function $\mathbb{P}$

questions.question: Which of the following always determines the whole distribution of a real-valued random variable $X$?
options: Its CDF $x\mapsto\mathbb{P}(X\le x)$ on all of $\mathbb{R}$
The set of values that $X$ can take
The probability $\mathbb{P}(X\le x)$ at one threshold $x$
The sample space $S$ on which $X$ is defined

questions.question: Let $X$ have density $1$ on $[0,1]$ and $Y$ have density $\frac{1}{2}$ on $[0,2]$, so $\mathbb{P}(X=x)=\mathbb{P}(Y=x)=0$ for every $x$. Do $X$ and $Y$ have the same distribution?
options: No; $\mathbb{P}(X\in[0,1])=1$ but $\mathbb{P}(Y\in[0,1])=\frac{1}{2}$
Yes; they agree on the probability of every single value
Yes; both put total probability $1$ on $[0,2]$
It cannot be decided without the sample space of each

questions.question: A fair die is rolled once, with outcome $\omega\in\{1,2,\ldots,6\}$, and $X(\omega)=|\omega-2|$. What is $\mathbb{P}(X\in\{1,3\})$?
